page: Amazon Web Services z1d.3xlarge is a memory-optimized instance engineered for applications requiring high sustained clock speeds alongside dense memory allocations. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8151 processor on the AWS Nitro System, the instance delivers 12 dedicated vCPUs across 6 physical cores at a fixed frequency of 4.0 GHz. The underlying x86_64 architecture incorporates 24 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and instruction set support for AVX, AVX-512, and AES-NI hardware-accelerated cryptography.

Memory capacity is configured with 96.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, providing an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. This provides ample capacity for memory-intensive computations without memory starvation. Local high-speed persistence is bundled as a single 450 GB NVMe SSD instance store volume, complemented by a baseline network throughput of 5 Gbps. No hardware accelerators or GPUs are provisioned on this configuration.

Benchmark results place the instance consistently within the middle 50 percent across standard compute and memory evaluation suites. The high clock speed yields a Geekbench single-core score of 1316.0 and a multi-core score of 6701.0, paired with a PassMark CPU score of 14193.22. Memory performance shows 66.01 GB/sec on large uncached read sweeps and 36.39 GB/sec on write sweeps. High-frequency operations translate well to transactional performance, achieving 12.59 million Redis SET operations per second and 4668.02 in PassMark database operations, although prompt processing on larger language models remains weak at 19.32 tokens per second.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the hardware profile targets environments where per-core software licensing costs are high, as the 4.0 GHz clock speed maximizes single-thread output across a compact core count. Bundled high-speed NVMe storage further avoids separate disk volume overheads for temporary operational data. Primary workload matches include relational database engines, electronic design automation (EDA), in-memory caches, financial simulation modeling, and build compilation pipelines.
description: Amazon Web Services z1d.3xlarge is a memory-optimized instance that pairs high sustained CPU frequency with substantial memory density. Built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8151 processor, it provides 12 vCPUs (6 physical cores) operating at 4.0 GHz, 96.0 GB of DDR4 memory, and a 450 GB NVMe SSD local drive alongside 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Synthetic benchmarks show steady mid-tier execution with a single-core Geekbench score of 1316.0 and 12.59 million Redis SET operations per second. The 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio and high clock speed maximize performance in core-licensed environments, making it suitable for relational databases, in-memory caching layers, EDA tooling, and software compilation.
